correctness.rationale: Exact distance-difference identity converts failure to resolve into existence of a nonzero ternary null vector. A 3x3 sign minor is zero or plus/minus four; the signed-cofactor construction proves every <=3-rank sign system has such a vector. Thus four-cube metric bases are exactly invertible 4x4 sign-row sets. The 1820 four-subsets, allowed slides and all 928 BFS roots are exhaustively reproduced by direct-profile C++17 and independent ternary-kernel/automorphism Python 3 checks. Both compute 928 vertices, 3584 edges, one component, degree counts (7:512,8:384,16:32), eccentricity counts (8:64,9:592,10:272), eight cube-symmetry orbits and radius 8/diameter 10. The finite case is exhaustive, with no unsupported infinite claim.

value.rationale: All four-landmark bases on the canonical tesseract are the natural complete state space of minimum-distance landmark placement. Restricted one-edge sensor relocation under continuous resolvability is a motivated reconfiguration task distinct from unconstrained matroid base exchange. Exact connectivity, radius 8, diameter 10, all orbit populations and eccentricities reveal structurally inequivalent local mobility, notably two maximum-degree classes with different eccentricities. This is not an arbitrary unmotivated slice or a recollection of the known metric dimension; it is an exact small benchmark with a complete structural metric profile.
